question: Does any benefit from function-preserving expert noise require a learned conditional router, rather than frozen random routing or ordinary dense parameter-noise regularization?
hypothesis: A genuinely conditional upcycling effect will exceed both a frozen-router MoE control and an exact-total-parameter-matched dense-wide noise control at the same bank size and noise scale, with route reliance above 0.01 and no more than two ID points lost.
predicted_signature: The learned MoE improves OOD-validation mean or worst-experiment accuracy over both controls from epoch 30 to 60 while frozen routing and dense-wide noise do not reproduce its route reliance.
alternative_explanation: Symmetry-breaking acts as generic optimization noise or ensemble-like total capacity, so frozen-router or dense-wide controls reproduce the apparent gain.
falsifier: Frozen-router or dense-wide controls match the learned-MoE movement, or every learned/noise cell remains at route reliance at or below 0.01.
pruning_rule: At epoch 10 prune a control dominated on OOD validation, ID retention, worst-experiment accuracy, and its predeclared mechanism signature unless differentiation is increasing; continue to 60 only for a competitive epoch-30 trajectory or route reliance above 0.01.
checkpoint_policy: save epochs 10, 30, and 60 for every arm reaching the milestone
multiplicity: Exploratory mechanism-control family opened after broad architecture, pressure, expert-count, temperature, auxiliary, and noise searches; no winner is confirmatory without a locked fresh seed.
